collection.description: A summer storm rolls in after dark, smelling of hot stone and green rain.

ask.text:
A summer storm rolls in after dark, smelling of hot stone and green rain. The palms bend and whip like dancers who have had too much to drink, and the whole village is shut up tight. Except (subject) and (friend), who both decided it was too hot to sleep inside and strung their hammocks between the same two palms on the beach. Both of them sleep through everything.
At midnight a bolt of lightning strikes the sand between the hammocks with a crack that shakes every hut on the island.
In the morning, (subject) wakes up, yawns, and finds (subject.himself/herself) looking at (subject)'s own face, snoring in the other hammock. (friend) wakes up a moment later and screams in (subject)'s voice.

c1o1.text: They sit there for three nights. On the third, the clouds come boiling back over the hills and the thunder rolls in like a wave. Both of them squeeze their eyes shut. CRACK! The lightning strikes the sand between them again, almost exactly where it struck before, and in the morning they're back in their own bodies, ears ringing and very glad of it. "Your knees are terrible," says (subject), rubbing (subject.his/her) own. "Your stomach is worse," says (friend). "What do you even eat?" They don't speak for a day, and then they laugh about it for the rest of their lives.

c1o2.text: They wait all through the stormy season. The rain comes, the wind comes, but the lightning never strikes the beach again. In the end (subject) and (friend) give up, and learn to live each other's lives. It is harder than either of them expected. (subject) finds out why (friend) always walks so slowly in the mornings. (friend) finds out why (subject) never sits on the left side of the fire. By the end of the season they know more about each other than anyone else in the village, and they argue less than they used to, which their families find very strange.

c1.text: The healers have never heard of anything like it. The elders say lightning took them, so lightning must give them back. That evening (subject) and (friend) sit back to back on the sand between the two palms, under a sky that is, very annoyingly, clear...

c2o1.text: They each try the other's job for a day, with a great deal of shouting across the village for advice. "Which end of this do I hold?" "The END THAT ISN'T SHARP!" By evening they're both exhausted and oddly proud of themselves. It goes so well that they do it again the next day, and the next. They never do swap back, and after a while they stop trying. Both of them end up better at the other one's work than they ever were at their own.

c2o2.text: By midday they can't stand it. (subject) keeps tripping over (friend)'s feet and (friend) keeps eating (subject)'s lunch "because this stomach is always hungry." They march to the healers together and demand that something be done. The healers mix up something thick, grey and bubbling and make them drink every drop. It tastes like a swamp. It smells worse. But in the time it takes to stop gagging, each of them is back behind their own eyes. Neither of them can taste anything for a week, and from then on neither of them will go near the healers' hut unless they're carried.

c2.text: "Well," says (friend), in (subject)'s voice. "We can't go anywhere like this. Could be worse. I've always wondered what you actually do all day." (subject) looks down at (friend)'s hands, and has to admit (subject.he/she) has wondered the same...
